children: Shares of European defense companies are in decline after a mixed set of quarterly results and midterm election results that cast doubt on the extent of U.S. military spending going forward. Investors are concerned that Democrats' win of majorities in both chambers of Congress could jeopardize defense bills from which European contractors can also benefit through contracts to supply the U.S. armed forces. In Germany, Rheinmetall shares are down 17% after a second guidance downgrade, with Renk Group shares down 6% and Hensoldt's down 2%. France's Thales is down 0.9%. In Italy, Leonardo shares are down 2.8% even though the company raised its annual order guidance for the second time. The U.K.'s BAE Systems sheds 3%. (mauro.orru@wsj.com)
